 Bodum Recalls 5.9 Million French Presses After Burn Reports
 Daily Coffee News Staff | October 29, 2026 
 A Bodum Chambord French press. Additional recalled product images and information are available through the CPSC recall notice .
 Bodum USA is recalling approximately 5.9 million French press coffee makers in the United States sold during a 52-year span.
 The recall follows 70 reports of glass carafes breaking during use, including 48 reports of burns to consumers.
 The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) announced the recall today, Oct. 29, warning that damaged or cracked glass carafes can break unexpectedly during use, posing a risk of serious burn injuries.
 The recall involves 8-cup and 12-cup French press coffee makers with replaceable glass carafes from eight Bodum models: Bistro, Brazil, Caffettiera, Chambord, Crema, Java, Jesper and Kenya.
 According to the CPSC, the glass carafes can become damaged through the use of metal spoons or other metal utensils to stir coffee, potentially leading to breakage during subsequent use.
 The affected coffee makers were sold from 1974 through October 2026 at Target, Walmart and coffee and home goods stores nationwide, as well as through Amazon, Bodum’s website and other online retailers. Retail prices ranged from approximately $15 to $65.
 The Bodum name appears on the frame and inner lid of most affected models and is engraved on the glass carafes along with product warnings. The coffee makers were manufactured in Portugal and Thailand and imported by New York-based Bodum USA.
 The recall remedy does not include refunds or replacement coffee makers. Instead, Bodum is providing affected consumers with a plastic stirring spoon and a warning label. The company is instructing owners to immediately stop using metal utensils to stir coffee in the glass carafes and to avoid using carafes that are cracked or damaged.
 Consumers can request the recall remedy through Bodum’s dedicated recall website or by calling 888-879-8213 from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern time, Monday through Friday.
 The full CPSC recall notice includes photos of affected coffee makers and additional product identification information.
